events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.43 (model confidence 0.75)
events.body:
Safety screen first: I read the full chat record [F10] including the driver's message [F8], the rider's reply [F9], the driver's post-trip statement [F11] and the rider's complaint. Nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or an allegation of dangerous driving — this is a fare/route argument only. Safety concern: none, per SAFE-1 and SAFE-2.

The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride (complaint header "charged $39.18 (metered)"; itemisation of base, distance, time, meter waiting and platform fee [F7]), so excess mileage feeds directly into what the rider pays and the RydeTAXI branch of RD-2 applies, as rider C1 frames it [F7][RD-2]. RD-1 is satisfied on the trace: exactly one off-route segment exists [F3], 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, +4.56 km, up to 1958 m off route, in a trip of 18.7 km against a 13.9 km optimal route [F1][F3][RD-1].

RD-4 gives no excuse. No traffic incident was recorded on the replaced stretch in the trip window [F14], and the recorded road bands are band 5, 40–49 km/h, i.e. flowing [F12][F13], so neither RD-4(a) nor RD-4(b) excuses the segment — a finding both sides accept [F14][RD-4].

RD-3 does not excuse it either. The rider never named a place: the place ("the petrol station just ahead") was named by the driver in his own request [F8], and the rider's "Sure, no problem." [F9] accepts a stop, not a destination — the trace confirms no stop was measured in the segment, so the premise of RD-3(a) (a rider-named place where the car stopped) is absent [F9][RD-3]. RD-3(b)/(c) are therefore not engaged on consent; the stop's timing treatment under RD-3(c) leaves the $0.11 meter waiting unit untouched, as both parties concede [F5][RD-3].

RD-5 is the decisive question, and it is answered against the driver. The rider's message [F9] was sent at 21:36, before the segment began at 21:39 [F3][F10], so its timing qualifies, but the scope of the words does not cover this segment. "Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute?" [F8] asks for a stop, not for a route, and "Sure, no problem." [F9] agrees to that stop. That is neither a general route authorisation ("whichever way is faster", which would still not cover a stop away from the route of the driver's own choosing) nor a specific named road — no road or area is named anywhere in the chat, so there is nothing for the record to tie the 4.56 km segment to, and instead of an untied named road the record places the excursion somewhere the rider never agreed to: a 6.27 km, 10-minute loop reaching 1958 m off the optimal route [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. The agreement to a one-minute stop is a "something else" and the segment counts (RD-5, scope of consent). The driver's own statement that "the rider agreed to a short stop so I thought a small change of route was fine" [F11] is a post-trip claim about the scope of his own route choice; even setting G11 aside, it describes a "small change" that the measurement contradicts [F11][F3][RD-5]. F10 confirms the chat record is complete and every message timestamped, so this is not an RD-5/G12 timing gap; the record settles the segment as unexempted, and the case does not need to go to a person for that element.

Amount: RD-2 refunds Σ unexempted extra_km × the trip's per-km rate, and the rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $26.31 ÷ 18.66 km = $1.4100/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The unexempted segment added 4.56 km [F3], so 4.56 km × $1.4100/km = $6.4296 → $6.43. The billed excess of $6.77 on 4.80 km [F4] exceeds the segment's extra km by 0.24 km of unmatched mileage, which RD-2 expressly does not refund (map-matching jitter and in-corridor mileage), so the refund is capped at the segment figure, as both briefs ultimately accept [F4][F3][RD-2]. The $0.11 meter waiting unit is kept under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3], and no other unpublished add-on appears [F6][F7], so no FARE-1 refund arises and FARE-2 is not triggered (no tolls field) [F7][FARE-1].

Account action: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days for the repeated-breach flag. The driver's profile shows 4 disputes with 2 upheld but 0 route disputes upheld [F17], and the rider's profile shows no upheld disputes either [F16]; the trace marks this element ✗, so no flag_account attaches and none is set. The finding of an RD-1 breach is recorded, and the refund is issued as a voucher per NS-7 [F3][RD-6][NS-7].

events.body:
✓ ruling consistent with the policy certificate
model confidence 0.75 (diagnostic only; automation is decided by the certificate)
certificate: ✓ RD-1 off-route segment(s) exist [case] 1 segment(s) (F3)
✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F3] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (no evidence)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 21:39:55 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 21:35 driver: “Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute? Tank is almost empty.”; F9: Chat #2 21:36 rider: “Sure, no problem.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “The rider agreed to a short stop so I thought a small change of route was fine.” (F8, F9, F11)

? RD-3 rider-requested stop; whether the rider named this place [F3] RULE (RD-3(a)): exempt if a RIDER message before the segment named a specific place and the car stopped there (the whole way there is exempt; how long the stop lasted or how far the place was does not reduce it). A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F8, F9)
✗ RD-6 prior upheld route dispute in 90 d (repeated breach → flag_account) [case] route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (F17)

? SAFE-1 safety screen: any threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the chat, statement or complaint [case] answer in safety_concern (none / suspected / confirmed) with safety_basis; suspected or confirmed → escalate. no hint word; read the messages anyway, a threat needs no keyword (no evidence)
allowed outcomes: refund_partial, no_action, escalate; amount = Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km (distance_fare ÷ distance_km), rounded to cents
flag_account required: False
